question: Do vacuum and one-local-fault first-flux representatives admit bounded exact first-public laws and informative structural omitted-error certificates under the inherited cap?

hypotheses.feasible: Both representative complete first records have positive exact base likelihood and their two 8,192-error sector priors and one-site omitted upper bounds close within the inherited budget.
hypotheses.censored: A representative has incompatible first charge, excessive projector work, or a loose omitted bound; retain the negative feasibility result without expanding the budget.

frozen_model: R6AF ideal periodic L=2 D4 geometry/orbit, 36 IID red-X physical edges at p_X=1/10 and p_Z=0. The first observation is the J6O pre-action complete 24-bit flux/charge/vacuum record, signal-only with vacuum=1-charge. The two fixed relation-free public charge actions [0] and [1,30,32,34,35] remain reserved for later action-bound second-record tests; neither is run here. Physical error support remains private to generation/scoring and is never an action input. No histories, noisy readout, logical score, second public law, or policy is evaluated.

matrix.independent_unit: One of 8,192 distinct private red-X supports per representative flux sector; exact rational enumeration with no stochastic uncertainty.
matrix.bound: All eligible first-star projectors must pairwise commute. The complete all-zero charge record is contained in each one-site event. A deterministic negative site gives zero likelihood; otherwise a fair one-site marginal bounds likelihood by 1/2, or all deterministic positive sites by 1. For base joint mass A and prior-weighted omitted upper U, omitted posterior is at most U/(A+U).
matrix.integrity: Pin inputs and runner, assert GF(2) rank 23/nullity 13, 8,192 unique physical errors in each distinct flux, flux different from J8I selected flux, eligible-site consistency, first-star commutation, exact IID normalization and prior partition, full-binary vacuum convention, positive exact base first likelihood, input hashes before/after, and term/CPU caps. Fail closed on mismatch.

acceptance: Two distinct other-flux exact sector priors and representative complete first-record base laws with exact rational one-site omitted upper certificates
No extrapolation from the two representatives to all other flux sectors or full-IID information/risk
Zero second laws, histories, arms, bootstraps and new dependencies
stop_rule: Stop after the two representative sectors or first integrity/CPU/65,536-term failure. A loose certificate is a negative feasibility result; do not add sectors, fit a crossing/threshold, or infer information/risk.
